name: Streamer channels
description: A channel of your favourite Twitch and YouTube streamers, in priority order: whoever is live is shown (the highest in the list wins), with their chat and pop-ups when the others are live too. While nobody is live, a countdown to the next stream, predicted from their past ones. No API keys needed. Needs Chrome or Edge on this computer, and yt-dlp (downloaded for you).
author: SchedularrTV
lowPowerNotice: a live or replayed stream is the heaviest kind of channel there is: the stream is decoded in software, the chat and pop-ups are drawn as see-through frames over it, and the result is encoded again. Expect one such channel at a time at most, at 480p or 360p and 5 to 8 capture frames per second. The countdown while nobody is live is light.

settings.label: yt-dlp
settings.description: Opens the streams. Leave empty to use the copy downloaded on the Streamers page, or one installed on this computer.

settings.label: Browser
settings.description: Chrome, Edge or Chromium, run hidden to draw the countdown, the chat and the pop-ups. Leave empty to find one automatically.
settings.lowPowerNote: On Raspberry Pi OS, install chromium (sudo apt install chromium); Chrome and Edge have no ARM Linux builds.

settings.label: ffmpeg
settings.description: Leave empty to use the ffmpeg set under App settings.

settings.label: Stream address
settings.description: How ErsatzTV reaches this scheduler. Leave empty unless ErsatzTV runs on another machine or in a container.

settings.label: Check who's live every (seconds)
settings.description: 20 to 900. A streamer counts as offline after two checks in a row say so.
settings.lowPowerNote: Each check fetches every streamer's page; every two minutes or more (the default here) keeps it light.

settings.label: Highest stream quality
settings.description: The tallest picture asked of a stream. The channel itself is 720p, so more mostly costs bandwidth.
settings.lowPowerNote: Use 480 or 360 here: the stream is decoded in software, and a 720p60 stream alone can take most of the processor. Avoid 1080.

settings.label: Time zone for predictions
settings.description: Streamers' habits ("Saturdays at 8pm") are worked out in this time zone, e.g. America/New_York. Leave empty for this computer's.

settings.label: Capture frames per second
settings.description: How often the chat and pop-ups are drawn (5 to 30). The stream itself always plays at its own rate.
settings.lowPowerNote: Keep this at 5 to 8 here: each frame is a full see-through picture the browser draws and ffmpeg decodes.

settings.label: Decode streams on the graphics chip
settings.description: Let the graphics chip decode the live stream or replay instead of the processor (ffmpeg's -hwaccel): usually the biggest saving after encoding. auto picks one if there is one; cuda is NVIDIA, qsv Intel, d3d11va any card on Windows, vaapi Intel or AMD on Linux, videotoolbox a Mac. A stream it can't decode is decoded in software instead. To encode on the graphics chip too, choose its encoder under App settings, Hardware and video encoding, Live page channels.
settings.lowPowerNote: The Pi's chip decodes HEVC but not H.264 this way, and Twitch and YouTube streams are H.264, so this saves little here.

settings.label: Keep a channel running after its last viewer (seconds)
settings.description: Holds the stream over guide changes, when ErsatzTV briefly reconnects.
